pain: The spec's concurrency, failed-commit and corruption scenarios are only proven with independent processes and real storage failure.
who: HOME's trusted internal consumers: Collectors that append Activity Events and Projections that replay them.
done_when: Race tests use child_process.fork writers on one temporary database file, not threads or a single connection.
8 writers racing one Event Key with different subjects give exactly one appended and the rest conflict, over 20 rounds.
4 writers making 200 distinct appends each give sequences 1 to 800 and verifyHistory passes.
A test-installed SQLite trigger that aborts an insert makes the append throw with no receipt and an unchanged head; after the trigger is dropped the same append gets the next sequence.
A writer killed with SIGKILL during an append loop leaves a ledger that verifyHistory accepts after reopen.
A writer that commits and exits without reporting is followed by a retry that returns duplicate with the committed receipt.
Edits to entry_json, sequence or previous_digest made through a raw connection with the triggers dropped are each reported by verifyHistory, and replayEffectiveHistory throws instead of replaying.
No production code has a test-only fault hook, and npm run check passes in CI on all three Node versions.

out_of_scope: Live Collectors and Identity Binding config
Projections, Activity Calendar and Project Timeline
Any HOME API, MCP server or Scope enforcement
Real customer or account data; fixtures are synthetic
Merges, deploys and paid model spend without Danny's yes
